precepts.text: Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not, when they defile my tabernacle; the defilement laws guarded the sacrifice.
precepts.point: The touching itself pertained to the sacrifice: Israel was separated from their uncleanness that they die not when they defile the tabernacle, so a man that had touched the unclean thing could not come in to sacrifice. There is no more sacrifice, so the touching-defilement laws do not apply today; a brush of boar bristles is not sin.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
The touching itself pertained to the sacrifice. “Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness; that they die not in their uncleanness, when they defile my tabernacle that is among them.” A man that had touched the unclean thing could not come in to sacrifice; the defilement laws guarded the tabernacle, that Israel die not.

Touching the carcase of an unclean beast or the uncleanness of man goes into eating, not mere contact. It is the same as telling your son or daughter, get your hand out of the cookie jar: you say do not touch it, not do not eat it, because you know what the intention is. The Lord deals with us the same way; do not be touching that stuff means do not eat it, do not defile yourself.

There is no more sacrifice, so the touching-defilement laws do not apply today; a brush of boar bristles is not sin.

precepts.text: Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not, when they defile my tabernacle; the uncleanness laws guarded the sacrifice.
precepts.point: All the touching of unclean and defiled things pertains to sacrifice: the point of the uncleanness laws was to separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not when they defile the tabernacle. There is no more sacrifice, so those defilement laws do not apply today; a brother can brush his hair with a brush of boar bristles, because that law was about coming in to sacrifice.

note.label: Leviticus 7: Christ Our Peace Offering

precepts.why:
All the touching of unclean and defiled things pertains to sacrifice. “Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness; that they die not in their uncleanness, when they defile my tabernacle that is among them.”

An unclean man coming into the tabernacle to sacrifice or a priest eating unclean was facing death before the Lord; that is why the flesh that touched any unclean thing was burnt with fire and the soul that ate of the peace offerings with his uncleanness upon him was cut off. The uncleanness laws guarded the sacrifice.

There is no more sacrifice, so those defilement laws do not apply today. A brother can brush his hair with a brush of boar bristles, because that law was about coming in to sacrifice.

precepts.text: If a woman have an issue of blood she shall be put apart seven days; those are the days of the separation.
precepts.point: The seven days match the law of the woman's issue: when her issue is blood, she is put apart seven days; those are the days of her separation spoken of here.

note.label: Leviticus 12: The Law of Purification After Childbirth

precepts.why:
When a woman has conceived seed and born a man child, “she shall be unclean seven days; according to the days of the separation for her infirmity shall she be unclean.” The seven days come from the law of the woman’s issue.

“And if a woman have an issue, and her issue in her flesh be blood, she shall be put apart seven days: and whosoever toucheth her shall be unclean until the even.” Those seven days she is put apart are the days of her separation, and the law of childbirth is measured by them: after a son, she is unclean the same seven days, as in her separation.

precepts.text: The law of her separation: she shall be put apart seven days.
precepts.point: A woman put apart for her uncleanness is a woman in her menstrual cycle. A man must wait the appointed seven days, and if the issue runs beyond, wait again; Leviticus 15 details these laws of uncleanness, taught in the previous class.

note.label: Leviticus 18: After the Doings of Egypt and Canaan Shall Ye Not Do

precepts.why:
A woman “put apart for her uncleanness” is a woman in her menstrual cycle. Leviticus 15 details these laws of uncleanness: “if a woman have an issue, and her issue in her flesh be blood, she shall be put apart seven days: and whosoever toucheth her shall be unclean until the even.”

So a man must wait the appointed seven days, and if the issue runs beyond, wait again. Thou shalt not approach unto her as long as she is put apart.

precepts.text: The law of the woman put apart in her issue; chapter 20 judges what chapter 15 defines.
precepts.point: The nakedness of the mother's sister and the father's sister is near kin; they bear their iniquity. He that lies with his uncle's wife or takes his brother's wife, they shall die childless.

note.label: Leviticus 20: The Judgments Appointed for the Abominations

precepts.why:
“if a man shall lie with a woman having her sickness, and shall uncover her nakedness; he hath discovered her fountain, and she hath uncovered the fountain of her blood: and both of them shall be cut off from among their people.” Her sickness is her menstrual cycle.

Chapter 15 defines what chapter 20 judges: “if a woman have an issue, and her issue in her flesh be blood, she shall be put apart seven days: and whosoever toucheth her shall be unclean until the even.” She is put apart; to lie with her in that time is to discover her fountain, and both are cut off.

precepts.text: The law of the uncleanness that chanceth a man by night: he shall wash all his flesh in water and be unclean until the even.
precepts.point: Any man that was not clean by reason of uncleanness that chanceth him by night went abroad out of the camp; when evening came he washed himself with water, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
What is the uncleanness that chanceth a man by night? Leviticus gives the law of it: “And if any man’s seed of copulation go out from him, then he shall wash all his flesh in water, and be unclean until the even.”

That is the man of this law. Being unclean until the even, he went abroad out of the camp and did not come within it; when evening came he washed himself with water, as Leviticus commands, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again. The two laws are one: unclean until the even, washed in water, then back in the camp.

precepts.text: The priests could not deal with holy things while unclean, so they had to be clean before serving.
precepts.point: The Levites bore the ark upon their shoulders with the staves, as Moses commanded according to the word of the Most High.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 15: None Ought to Carry the Ark but the Levites

precepts.why:
“Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness; that they die not in their uncleanness, when they defile my tabernacle that is among them.” The priests could not deal with holy things while unclean, so they had to be clean before serving.

That is why David charged the chief of the fathers of the Levites, “sanctify yourselves, both ye and your brethren, that ye may bring up the ark of the Lord God of Israel unto the place that I have prepared for it.” “So the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves to bring up the ark of the Lord God of Israel.”

points: If any man's seed of copulation go out from him, he shall wash all his flesh in water and be unclean until the evening. If it touched any garment or skin, that had to be washed too. And when a man lay with his wife, they both had to bathe themselves in water and be unclean until the evening. So by the law, after sex you were unclean until evening.

note.label: Sexual Discipline

points: Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not in their uncleanness, when they defile my tabernacle that is among them. The tabernacle was the temple. So could you have sex and go up to the temple on the new moon or on the Sabbath? No, because you would be unclean, and you cannot go up to the temple unclean. The priests doing the service, and all of us, since it was a commandment to come up to the tabernacle and worship God every high holy day, had to control the sexual appetite. Our forefathers practiced sexual discipline.
Tonight is a feast day, but this is not the tabernacle, so that law does not apply today, and we are not going to put that burden on you. But it shows you the discipline that was required.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: Every bed whereon he lies and every thing whereon he sits is unclean. Whoever touches his bed, sits where he sat, touches his flesh, or is touched by him before he has rinsed his hands, washes his clothes, bathes himself in water, and is unclean until the even; the same goes for his spittle and his saddle.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: The vessel of earth that he touches shall be broken, and every vessel of wood shall be rinsed in water.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: When he that hath an issue is cleansed of his issue, he numbers to himself seven days for his cleansing, washes his clothes, and bathes his flesh in running water, and shall be clean.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: On the eighth day he takes two turtledoves or two young pigeons and comes before the Lord unto the door of the tabernacle, and gives them unto the priest; the priest offers the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, and makes an atonement for him before the Lord for his issue.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: If any man's seed of copulation go out from him, he washes all his flesh in water and is unclean until the even; every garment and every skin whereon is the seed is washed with water and unclean until the even.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: The woman also with whom a man lies with seed of copulation: they both bathe themselves in water and are unclean until the even.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: When a woman has an issue, and her issue in her flesh be blood, she is put apart seven days for her separation, and whosoever toucheth her is unclean until the even.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: Every thing that she lies upon or sits upon in her separation is unclean; whoever touches her bed or any thing she sat upon washes his clothes, bathes himself in water, and is unclean until the even.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: If any man lie with her at all, and her flowers be upon him, he is unclean seven days, and all the bed whereon he lies is unclean.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: If a woman have an issue of her blood many days out of the time of her separation, or if it run beyond the time of her separation, all the days of the issue of her uncleanness are as the days of her separation: she is unclean.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: Every bed she lies on and every thing she sits upon in those days is as the uncleanness of her separation, and whosoever touches those things washes his clothes, bathes in water, and is unclean until the even.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: When she is cleansed of her issue, she numbers to herself seven days, and after that she shall be clean.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: On the eighth day she takes two turtles or two young pigeons and brings them unto the priest to the door of the tabernacle; the priest offers the one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, and makes an atonement for her before the Lord for the issue of her uncleanness.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: The purpose of the whole chapter is stated plainly: thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not in their uncleanness when they defile the tabernacle of the Most High that is among them.

note.label: Leviticus 15: The Law of Issues and Separation

points: This is the law of him that hath an issue, of him whose seed goeth from him, of her that is sick of her flowers, of him and her that have issues, and of him that lieth with her that is unclean.
